principles: Core customer and MCP field outlet are different identities.
Historical field activity remains attached to field outlet identity after linking.
No legacy identifier becomes canonical without evidence and reconciliation.
Mappings are installation-scoped, auditable and conflict-checked.
Every source identity is the composite key (installation, legacy id).

mappings.conflictPolicy: no automatic merge on name-only match
mappings.unmappedAction: retain service attribution and queue manual identity reconciliation

mappings.conflictPolicy: deduplicate only with deterministic rule and evidence
mappings.unmappedAction: block cutover for affected field lifecycle

requiredEvidence: approved onboarding or explicit link-existing decision
mappings.conflictPolicy: multiple outlets may link to one Core customer; one outlet cannot link to multiple active customers
mappings.unmappedAction: allow visits/tests/reports; forbid official Sales Order

requiredEvidence: address match or approved address creation
mappings.conflictPolicy: address must belong to linked Core customer
mappings.unmappedAction: forbid delivery-address use on official order

mappings.conflictPolicy: name-only match is insufficient for official order migration
mappings.unmappedAction: classify demand as intent/history or reconciliation required

mappings.conflictPolicy: ambiguous records are invalid/orphan until manually resolved

forbiddenShortcuts: bulk insert legacy orders into sales.sales_orders
treat nullable legacy customer_id as canonical customer proof
rewrite historical visit identity after customer linking
store provider identifiers in browser business logic
